messages:
anya: quick perf note from today's profiling run — host-side WCPU is ~38% of end-to-end p95 for short chat requests (<=128 tokens). flamegraph attached in thread. main suspects: tokenization, request parsing, and tiny gRPC writes.

sam: can you paste the top hotspots? was this with kvcache enabled? :thinking:

anya: kvcache ON (default), batch size steady at 1. here's the trimmed top-of-stack from the pprof (host proxy):

```
# top 10 by flat
  13.5%  token::tokenize::split_chunks
  10.9%  grpc::writev::emit_small_writes
   8.0%  parser::http::parse_headers
   4.8%  alloc::vec::grow
   4.2%  streaming::chunker::frame_and_send
```

anya: full run also shows a lot of tiny allocations during header parsing that correlate with the writev bursts. reproducible on the 8 GPU dev pool with replay workload.

kevin: wow 13.5% on tokenize.split_chunks is higher than I expected. are we tokenizing at the ingress side or deferring to the model? which tokenizer implementation was used? (rustshim vs python shim)

anya: rustshim v2 (recent default). we do host-side tokenization to avoid extra round trips for small prompts. but we might be paying for copy/alloc churn.

maria: two quick ideas: 1) micro-batch prefix tokenization — cache prefix tokens per client for repeated prompts; 2) pre-reserve buffers for header parsing to avoid vec grow.

sam: +1. Also noticed in the trace that streaming chunker creates a new iovec per token chunk instead of coalescing — that explains writev bursts. we can try a small coalescer to combine contiguous small frames before syscall.

infra-bot: perf-run 2026-03-20T12:03Z: replay=50k requests, kvcache hitrate=78%, avg batch=1.05, model latency median=12ms, host-side median=4.5ms

kevin: ^ the kvcache hitrate is decent but not great for these short chats. prefix caching might push hitrate up and reduce host CPU because fewer parse/token cycles.

anya: experiment plan:
- add a single-threaded small-write coalescer in host proxy (opt-in flag)
- change tokenizer to reuse a thread-local Vec<u8> buffer and avoid grow on common sizes
- add prefix hash cache with 5s TTL for frequent short prompts
- run A/B with coalescer on 10% traffic

jeff: +1 on rollout. quick perf caveat: coalescer needs a cap and latency escape hatch (don’t block behind waiting to coalesce). maybe a time-based flush @200us or size cap @8k.

maria: for allocs, we can also try jemalloc tcache tune for small allocs in the proxy process and measure delta.

sam: will draft a PR for buffer reuse + coalescer prototype tonight. can we instrument the proxy for small-write stats (writes < 1k, count, avg iovecs)? that'll make it easier to quantify.

anya: yes please. add new metrics: host.writev.count_small, host.writev.avg_iov_small, host.tokenize.alloc_count. want the first run in devpool by EOD tomorrow.

kevin: if prototype looks good, we should add a kernel-selection hint: when average seq len < 64 and batch==1 pick kernel path optimized for small seqs — avoids oversized kernel overhead. but that's a model-runtime change, ping eng-runtime + runtime team.

maria: noted. i'll coordinate with runtime team for the kernel hint API. also let's add a perf-test that replays high-frequency short prompts to catch regressions in CI.

anya: awesome. thanks all. leaving notes in the perf doc and will attach the flamegraph and a 20s trace. @sam please link PR here when ready :rocket:

sam: will do. starting with buffer reuse and small-write counter.

kevin: thanks, team — good incremental wins here :thumbsup:
